sentences.text: Ram Rajak vs Unknown on 7 July, 2025
Author: Debangsu Basak Bench: Debangsu Basak 07.07.2025 S.D. C.R.A. (DB)/ 79 of 2022

In the matter of : Ram Rajak ...... Appellant Mr. Tapan Dutta Gupta Mr. Parvej Alam Ms. Rituparna Ghosh Mr. Sourav Sarda ...for the appellant Ms. Zareen N. Khan Mr. Ashok Das ....for the State Appeal is heard at length in presence of the appellant.
Learned advocate appearing for the appellant repeatedly points out that three persons were charged at the trial.
Evidence as against three accused were evaluated to arrive at a finding that two are to be acquitted.
He submits that the appellant before the High Court, therefore, needs to be acquitted also on the basis of the same evidence as against the two other persons.
He relies upon AIR 1975 SC 1962 (Balaka Singh & Ors. Vs. The State of Punjab) in support of such proposition.

entities.text: AIR 1975 SC 1962 (Balaka Singh & Ors. Vs. The State of Punjab)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned advocate appearing for the State submits that since the appellant is of the view that two persons were acquitted on the basis of the same evidence, it would be appropriate that the Court hears the two acquitted persons also after issuance of a Rule.
Three persons stood trial, inter alia, on the charge of 498A/302 of the IPC, 1860.
At the trial, the charge under Section 498A as against all the accused were found not be proved.
As against three accused, charge of murder stood proved as against the appellant while the two others who are the parents-in-law of the victim were acquitted.

Since the appellant insists that he is entitled to a judgment of acquittal in view of the acquittal of parents-in-law of the victim and as the appellant is on the same footing, it would be appropriate to issue a Rule calling upon the two other accused in the trial to show-cause as to why the judgment of acquittal as against them be not reversed, if the material on record establishes their involvement.
Balaka (supra) was delivered in a trial relating to murder.

It is of the view that Court must make attempt to separate grain from chaff where case of the convicted accused is not severable from that of the acquitted accused, the entire prosecution must be discarded.
We are yet to arrive at a final decision with regard to the merits of the appeal.
It would be appropriate to hear all the accused before the trial.
List the appeal along with the rule on July 23, 2025.

(Debangsu Basak, J.) (Prasenjit Biswas, J.)
